rulers.title: Carthaginian generals and suffetes of note

list.name: Hamilcar son of Mago
list.note: Magonid commander in Sicily; killed at Himera (480) by Gelon; Herodotus says he threw himself into the sacrificial fire.

list.name: Hannibal son of Gisco (Mago)
list.note: Grandson of Hamilcar; destroyed Selinus and Himera (409), took Acragas; died of plague in the siege camp (406).

list.name: Himilco son of Hanno
list.note: Took Acragas and Gela; besieged Syracuse (397-396), army struck by plague, abandoned his mercenaries; starved himself at Carthage.

list.name: Mago (fl. 396-375)
list.note: Fought Dionysius I; killed at Cabala (c. 375).

list.name: Hanno the Great (4th c.)
list.note: Leading statesman who attempted a coup; crucified with his family (c. 350, Justin 21.4).

list.name: Hamilcar son of Gisco
list.note: Defeated Agathocles at the Himeras (311) and besieged Syracuse; captured in a night attack and beheaded (309).

list.name: Bomilcar
list.note: Commander against Agathocles in Africa; attempted to seize sole power (308); crucified in the agora.

list.name: Hanno (264)
list.note: Commander who surrendered the Messana citadel to the Romans; crucified at Carthage.

list.name: Hanno son of Hannibal
list.note: Commanded at Agrigentum (262), defeated and fined.

list.name: Hamilcar (First Punic War)
list.note: Victor at Thermae (260) and commander at Ecnomus (256).

list.name: Xanthippus
list.note: Spartan mercenary who reorganized the army and destroyed Regulus at the Bagradas (255), then left Carthage.

list.name: Adherbal
list.note: Admiral who destroyed Publius Claudius Pulcher's fleet at Drepana (249), Carthage's greatest naval victory.

list.name: Hanno (Aegates)
list.note: Admiral defeated by Lutatius Catulus at the Aegates Islands (10 Mar 241); crucified.

list.name: Hamilcar Barca
list.note: Commander in Sicily (247-241), victor of the Mercenary War (241-237), conqueror of southern Iberia (237-229); drowned crossing a river near Helike while retreating from the Oretani (229/228).

list.name: Hanno the Great (3rd c.)
list.note: Leader of the landed faction opposed to the Barcids and to the war with Rome; commander in the Mercenary War.

list.name: Gisco
list.note: Commander at Lilybaeum who evacuated the army; tortured to death by the rebel mercenaries Spendius and Mathos.

list.name: Hasdrubal the Fair
list.note: Barcid son-in-law; founded Carthago Nova (c. 227); the Ebro treaty with Rome (226/225); killed by a Celtic slave whose master he had executed.

list.name: Hannibal Barca
list.note: Commander in Iberia 221, invaded Italy 218, recalled 203, lost at Zama 202; suffete 196 (reformed the court of 104 and state finances); fled 195; poisoned himself at Libyssa in Bithynia c. 183.

list.name: Hasdrubal Barca
list.note: Commander in Iberia; crossed the Alps 207; killed at the Metaurus, his head thrown into Hannibal's camp.

list.name: Mago Barca
list.note: Commander at Trebia and Cannae, then in Iberia and Liguria (205-203); died of wounds at sea on recall.

list.name: Hasdrubal son of Gisco
list.note: Commander in Iberia, defeated at Ilipa (206); father of Sophonisba; routed at the Great Plains (203); poisoned himself (202) or was killed by a mob.

list.name: Hanno son of Bomilcar
list.note: Hannibal's subordinate in southern Italy; defeated at Beneventum (214).

list.name: Hasdrubal the Boeotarch
list.note: Commander in the Third Punic War; surrendered to Scipio Aemilianus at the Byrsa; his wife killed their children and threw herself into the burning temple of Eshmun.
list.death: survived as a captive in Italy

rulers.note: Carthage was a republic: 'from/to' are years of attested command or office, not reigns. role = suffete, general, or both.

list.name: Gelon
list.note: Deinomenid tyrant of Gela, then Syracuse; victor of Himera (480).

list.name: Hieron I
list.note: Victor over the Etruscans at Cumae (474); patron of Pindar and Aeschylus.

list.name: Thrasybulus
list.note: Expelled after 11 months; democracy restored.

list.name: Dionysius I
list.note: Fought four wars with Carthage; extended Syracusan power into southern Italy and the Adriatic.

list.name: Dionysius II
list.note: Expelled by Dion 357; regained the city 346; surrendered to Timoleon (344) and retired to Corinth.

list.name: Dion
list.note: Plato's friend; murdered by Callippus.

list.name: Timoleon
list.note: Corinthian liberator; defeated Carthage at the Crimisus (341); retired as a private citizen.

list.name: Agathocles
list.note: Tyrant from 317, king from 304; invaded Africa (310-307). Died 289, possibly poisoned.

list.name: Hicetas
list.note: Tyrant expelled by Thoenon.

list.name: Pyrrhus
list.note: King of Epirus invited as king of Sicily against Carthage; abandoned the island in 276.

list.name: Hieron II
list.note: General, then king (c. 270 after defeating the Mamertines at the Longanus); Rome's loyal ally from 263; Archimedes' patron. Died aged about 90.

list.name: Gelon II
list.note: Co-ruler with his father Hieron II; predeceased him.

list.name: Hieronymus
list.note: Grandson of Hieron II; switched to Carthage; assassinated at Leontini aged 15.

list.name: Hippocrates and Epicydes
list.note: Carthaginian-born brothers who led Syracuse against Rome until Marcellus took the city (212); Hippocrates died of plague, Epicydes fled to Agrigentum.

list.name: Pyrrhus (Epirus)
list.note: Earlier reign 307-302. Defeated Rome at Heraclea (280) and Asculum (279) at heavy cost, checked at Beneventum (275). Killed in street fighting at Argos, struck by a roof tile thrown by an old woman.

list.name: Antigonus I Monophthalmus
list.note: Took the royal title with Demetrius in 306; killed at Ipsus.

list.name: Demetrius I Poliorcetes
list.note: King of Macedon 294-288; surrendered to Seleucus 285.
list.death: drank himself to death in captivity in Syria

list.name: Antigonus II Gonatas
list.note: Claimed the title from 283; secured Macedon after defeating the Gauls at Lysimachia (277).

list.name: Demetrius II Aetolicus
list.note: Died fighting the Dardanians.

list.name: Antigonus III Doson
list.note: Regent then king; crushed Cleomenes III of Sparta at Sellasia (222).

list.name: Philip V
list.note: Allied with Hannibal (215); lost the Second Macedonian War at Cynoscephalae (197); executed his son Demetrius (180).

list.name: Perseus
list.note: Defeated at Pydna 22 Jun 168; walked in Aemilius Paullus' triumph.
list.death: died in custody at Alba Fucens, c. 166 (Diodorus says by sleep deprivation)

list.name: Andriscus (Philip VI)
list.note: Pretender claiming to be Perseus' son; defeated by Metellus (148), led in triumph and executed (146). Macedonia became a province.

rulers.title: Seleucid kings

list.name: Seleucus I Nicator
list.note: Satrap of Babylon 321/311 (Seleucid era from Oct 312); took the royal title 305; murdered by Ptolemy Keraunos near Lysimachia.

list.name: Antiochus I Soter
list.note: Co-king from 294; 'Elephant Victory' over the Galatians.

list.name: Antiochus II Theos
list.note: Died at Ephesus, allegedly poisoned by his first wife Laodice.

list.name: Seleucus II Callinicus
list.note: Lost the Third Syrian War and the east to the Parni; died falling from his horse.

list.name: Seleucus III Ceraunus
list.note: Killed by his officers on campaign in Asia Minor.

list.name: Antiochus III the Great
list.note: Eastern anabasis (212-205); took Coele-Syria at Panium (200); defeated by Rome at Thermopylae (191) and Magnesia (190); Peace of Apamea (188): 15,000 talents, Taurus frontier. Killed robbing the temple of Bel in Elymais.

list.name: Seleucus IV Philopator
list.note: Paid the Apamea indemnity; murdered by his minister Heliodorus.

list.name: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
list.note: Hostage at Rome; invaded Egypt (170-168) until Popillius Laenas drew the circle at Eleusis; persecution of Judaism provoked the Maccabean revolt. Died at Tabae in Persis.

list.name: Antiochus V Eupator
list.note: Boy king killed on the orders of Demetrius I.

list.name: Demetrius I Soter
list.note: Escaped from hostage in Rome with Polybius' help; killed against Alexander Balas.

list.name: Alexander I Balas
list.note: Pretender backed by Attalus II, Ptolemy VI and Rome; beaten at the Oenoparas, murdered in Arabia.

list.name: Demetrius II Nicator
list.note: Captured by the Parthians 138, released 129; killed at Tyre (125). First reign 145-138, second 129-125.

list.name: Antiochus VI Dionysus
list.note: Child king set up by Diodotus Tryphon, who killed him.

list.name: Diodotus Tryphon
list.note: General who made himself king; besieged at Apamea, killed himself or was killed.

list.name: Antiochus VII Sidetes
list.note: Took Jerusalem (134) and reconquered Babylonia; killed in a Parthian counter-attack in Media.

list.name: Alexander II Zabinas
list.note: Ptolemaic-backed pretender; executed by Antiochus VIII.

list.name: Cleopatra Thea
list.note: Queen of three kings; ruled alone 126-125; forced by Antiochus VIII to drink the poison she had prepared for him.

list.name: Seleucus V Philometor
list.note: Killed by his mother Cleopatra Thea.

list.name: Antiochus VIII Grypus
list.note: Killed by his minister Heracleon.

list.name: Antiochus IX Cyzicenus
list.note: Rival king in Coele-Syria; killed himself after defeat by Seleucus VI.

list.name: Seleucus VI Epiphanes
list.note: Burned alive in the gymnasium at Mopsuestia by the populace.

list.name: Antiochus X Eusebes
list.note: Killed fighting the Parthians or Philip I (date 92 or 88).

list.name: Demetrius III Eucaerus
list.note: Captured by the Parthians.

list.name: Antiochus XI Epiphanes
list.note: Drowned in the Orontes fleeing Antiochus X.

list.name: Antiochus XII Dionysus
list.note: Killed fighting the Nabataeans at Cana.

list.name: Tigranes II (in Syria)
list.note: The Armenian king held Syria until Lucullus' victory at Tigranocerta.

list.name: Antiochus XIII Asiaticus
list.note: Restored by Lucullus, rejected by Pompey; killed by the Emesene dynast Sampsiceramus.

list.name: Philip II Philoromaeus
list.note: Last claimant; Pompey annexed Syria (64/63).

rulers.note: Late Seleucid chronology (from c. 125 BC) is uncertain; dates follow Hoover's revisions where they differ.

rulers.title: Ptolemaic rulers of Egypt

list.name: Ptolemy I Soter
list.note: Satrap from 323; king 305/304; seized Alexander's body.

list.name: Ptolemy II Philadelphus
list.note: Co-regent 284; Museum and Library, Pharos; sent the first embassy to Rome (273).

list.name: Ptolemy III Euergetes
list.note: Third Syrian War; reached Babylon.

list.name: Ptolemy IV Philopator
list.note: Raphia (217), first large-scale use of Egyptian phalangites; native revolt in the Thebaid.

list.name: Ptolemy V Epiphanes
list.note: Lost Coele-Syria at Panium (200); Rosetta decree (196). Died possibly poisoned.

list.name: Ptolemy VI Philometor
list.note: Saved by Rome's ultimatum to Antiochus IV (168); died of wounds after the battle of the Oenoparas.

list.name: Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II (Physcon)
list.note: Co-king 170-164; king of Cyrene 163-145; willed Cyrene to Rome (155) in a famous inscription; civil war with Cleopatra II (132-124).

list.name: Ptolemy VII Neos Philopator
list.note: Killed by Ptolemy VIII at his own wedding to Cleopatra II (numbering disputed).

list.name: Cleopatra III
list.note: Co-ruled with her sons; killed by Ptolemy X (Justin).

list.name: Ptolemy IX Soter II (Lathyros)
list.note: Expelled 107 to Cyprus; restored 88-81.

list.name: Ptolemy X Alexander I
list.note: Killed in a naval battle off Cyprus after expulsion; reputedly bequeathed Egypt to Rome.

list.name: Berenice III
list.note: Murdered by her husband Ptolemy XI after 19 days of joint rule.

list.name: Ptolemy XI Alexander II
list.note: Installed by Sulla; lynched by the Alexandrians.

list.name: Ptolemy XII Neos Dionysos (Auletes)
list.note: Bought Roman recognition (6,000 talents to Caesar and Pompey, 59); expelled 58-55, restored by Gabinius.

list.name: Berenice IV
list.note: Ruled during her father's exile; executed on his return.

list.name: Cleopatra VII
list.note: Last Ptolemy; ally and lover of Caesar and Antony; killed herself in Alexandria c. 10/12 Aug 30.

list.name: Ptolemy XIII
list.note: Drowned in the Nile after defeat by Caesar.

list.name: Ptolemy XIV
list.note: Probably poisoned by Cleopatra (Josephus).

list.name: Ptolemy XV Caesarion
list.note: Son of Caesar and Cleopatra; killed on Octavian's orders ('too many Caesars').

rulers.note: Regnal numbering of Ptolemy VII and of the Cleopatras is conventional and debated.

list.name: Philetaerus
list.note: Eunuch commander who defected from Lysimachus with 9,000 talents.

list.name: Eumenes I
list.note: Defeated Antiochus I near Sardis.

list.name: Attalus I Soter
list.note: Took the royal title after defeating the Galatians (c. 238); Rome's ally against Philip V; brought the Magna Mater stone to Rome (205).

list.name: Eumenes II Soter
list.note: Gained most of Seleucid Asia Minor at Apamea (188); built the Great Altar.

list.name: Attalus II Philadelphus
list.note: Founded Attaleia; Stoa of Attalus at Athens.

list.name: Attalus III
list.note: Bequeathed his kingdom to Rome, which Tiberius Gracchus sought to use for his land programme.

list.name: Aristonicus (Eumenes III)
list.note: Claimed the throne and rallied slaves and the poor ('Heliopolitans'); captured by Perperna, strangled in Rome (128).

rulers.title: Mithridatid kings of Pontus

list.name: Pharnaces I
list.note: Took Sinope (183), his new capital.

list.name: Mithridates V Euergetes
list.note: Roman ally in the Third Punic War; assassinated at Sinope.

list.name: Mithridates VI Eupator
list.note: Fought three wars with Rome (89-85, 83-81, 73-63); massacre of Romans in Asia (88). Deposed by his son Pharnaces, poison failed (mithridatism), had his Gallic bodyguard Bituitus kill him at Panticapaeum.

list.name: Pharnaces II
list.note: King of the Bosporus; defeated by Caesar at Zela ('veni vidi vici', 2 Aug 47); killed by Asander.

rulers.note: Dates before Mithridates V are approximate.

list.name: Darius son of Pharnaces
list.note: Installed by Antony.

list.name: Polemon I
list.note: Antony's appointee kept by Augustus; also king of the Bosporus; killed fighting the Aspurgiani.

list.name: Pythodorida
list.note: Queen; granddaughter of Antony.

list.name: Polemon II
list.note: Pontus annexed by Nero (64) to Galatia/Cappadocia.

list.name: Zipoetes I
list.note: Ruler from c. 326, king 297; resisted Lysimachus and Antiochus I.

list.name: Nicomedes I
list.note: Invited the Galatians into Asia; founded Nicomedia (264).

list.name: Ziaelas
list.note: Killed by Galatian chiefs he had planned to murder.

list.name: Prusias I Cholus
list.note: Sheltered Hannibal; founded Prusa.

list.name: Prusias II Cynegus
list.note: Greeted Roman envoys dressed as a freedman; killed by his son Nicomedes.

list.name: Nicomedes III Euergetes
list.note: Told Marius that Roman tax-farmers had enslaved his subjects (104).

list.name: Nicomedes IV Philopator
list.note: Expelled by Mithridates twice (90-89, 88-84); his raid on Pontus at Roman urging triggered the First Mithridatic War; bequeathed Bithynia to Rome. Rumoured lover of the young Caesar.

list.name: Gaia
list.note: Father of Masinissa; Carthaginian ally.

list.name: Oezalces
list.note: Brother of Gaia, by agnatic succession.

list.name: Capussa
list.note: Killed by the rebel Mazaetullus.

list.name: Lacumazes
list.note: Puppet of Mazaetullus, expelled by Masinissa.

list.name: Masinissa
list.note: Regained his kingdom with Roman help, see numidia.

list.name: Syphax
list.note: Married Sophonisba and joined Carthage; captured by Laelius and Masinissa at Cirta (203).
list.death: died in Roman captivity at Tibur

list.name: Vermina
list.note: Son of Syphax; made peace with Rome (200).

list.name: Masinissa
list.note: United Numidia after Zama; reigned until about 90, constantly encroaching on Carthaginian land and provoking the Third Punic War.

list.name: Micipsa
list.note: Joint king with Gulussa and Mastanabal (Scipio Aemilianus divided the royal functions); sole king from c. 140; built up Cirta.

list.name: Gulussa
list.note: Held the military command.

list.name: Mastanabal
list.note: Held judicial functions; father of Jugurtha.

list.name: Hiempsal I
list.note: Killed by Jugurtha's agents at Thirmida.

list.name: Adherbal
list.note: Besieged in Cirta by Jugurtha; killed with the Italian traders of the city, provoking Rome's war.

list.name: Jugurtha
list.note: Betrayed by Bocchus I to Sulla (105); led in Marius' triumph.

list.name: Gauda
list.note: Half-brother of Jugurtha; Marius' client.

list.name: Hiempsal II
list.note: Expelled by the Marians (81-?) and restored by Pompey; author of Punic books used by Sallust.

list.name: Hiarbas
list.note: Marian-backed usurper; killed after Pompey's African campaign.

list.name: Juba I
list.note: Destroyed Curio's army at the Bagradas (49); after Thapsus he and Petreius fought a suicide duel at Zama. Kingdom became Africa Nova.

list.name: Baga
list.note: Provided Masinissa with 4,000 men (206).

list.name: Bocchus I
list.note: Father-in-law of Jugurtha whom he betrayed to Sulla; gained western Numidia.

list.name: Bogud
list.note: King of western Mauretania, Caesarian; fled to Antony when Tingis rebelled.

list.name: Bocchus II
list.note: East, then all Mauretania from 38; bequeathed it to Rome.

list.name: Juba II
list.note: Son of Juba I raised in Rome; married Cleopatra Selene; scholar-king at Iol Caesarea; wrote on Libya and Arabia (used by Pliny).

list.name: Ptolemy of Mauretania
list.note: Grandson of Antony and Cleopatra; summoned to Lugdunum and killed by Caligula, provoking the revolt of Aedemon and the annexation of two provinces (c. 42).

rulers.title: Kings of Armenia

list.name: Artaxias I
list.note: Former Seleucid strategos; founded Artaxata (with Hannibal's advice, per Strabo and Plutarch).

list.name: Tigranes II the Great
list.note: Built an empire from the Caucasus to Syria; founded Tigranocerta; defeated by Lucullus (69) and submitted to Pompey (66).

list.name: Artavasdes II
list.note: Abandoned Crassus; seized by Antony (34) and led in his Alexandrian triumph.

list.name: Artaxias II
list.note: Killed by his courtiers as Tiberius approached.

list.name: Tigranes III
list.note: Crowned by Tiberius.

list.name: Tigranes IV and Erato
list.note: Anti-Roman sibling-spouses; Tigranes killed in war c. AD 1.

list.name: Ariobarzanes
list.note: Median prince installed by Gaius Caesar.

list.name: Vonones
list.note: Ex-king of Parthia; removed under Parthian pressure.

list.name: Artaxias III (Zeno)
list.note: Son of Polemon I, crowned by Germanicus at Artaxata.

list.name: Arsaces
list.note: Son of Artabanus II.

list.name: Mithridates (of Iberia)
list.note: Reigned 35-37 and 42-51; murdered by his nephew Rhadamistus.

list.name: Rhadamistus
list.note: Iberian prince; expelled twice by the Armenians.

list.name: Tiridates I
list.note: Brother of Vologases I; crowned by Nero in Rome (66) after the compromise of Rhandeia (63): Parthian prince, Roman investiture. Reign interrupted by Tigranes VI (60-62).

list.name: Tigranes VI
list.note: Roman nominee imposed by Corbulo.

list.name: Axidares
list.note: Deposed by Osroes, provoking Trajan's war.

list.name: Parthamasiris
list.note: Laid his diadem at Trajan's feet at Elegeia; killed by his Roman escort. Armenia made a province (114-117).

list.name: Sohaemus
list.note: Roman senator and consul of Emesene/Arsacid descent; expelled by Vologases IV (161), restored by Statius Priscus (164).

list.name: Pacorus
list.note: Parthian appointee.

list.name: Khosrov I
list.note: Lured and imprisoned by Caracalla.

list.name: Tiridates II
list.note: Resisted the Sasanians.

list.name: Hormizd-Ardashir (Sasanian)
list.note: Shapur I's son as 'Great King of Armenia' during Persian occupation.

list.name: Narseh (Sasanian)
list.note: Later shahanshah.

list.name: Tiridates III
list.note: Restored by Rome; converted by Gregory the Illuminator (traditionally 301, more probably c. 314), making Armenia the first Christian kingdom. Dates disputed (some put the reign 298-330).

list.name: Tiran
list.note: Blinded by the Persians.

list.name: Arshak II
list.note: Wavered between Rome and Persia; imprisoned by Shapur II in the Fortress of Oblivion.

list.name: Pap
list.note: Installed by Valens; murdered at a banquet by the Roman general Trajanus (Amm. 30.1).

list.name: Arshak III
list.note: Ruled Roman Armenia after the partition of c. 387.

list.name: Khosrov IV
list.note: Persian Armenia.

list.name: Vramshapuh
list.note: Patron of Mesrop Mashtots and the Armenian alphabet (c. 405).

list.name: Artaxias IV (Artashir)
list.note: Deposed by Bahram V at the request of the Armenian nobles; Persarmenia became a marzpanate.

rulers.note: Artaxiad, then Roman/Parthian nominees, Arsacid from 66. Many 1st-3rd century dates are approximate; numbering follows modern convention.

rulers.title: Arsacid kings of Parthia

list.name: Arsaces I
list.note: Leader of the Parni; Arsacid era begins 247.

list.name: Arsaces II
list.note: Submitted to Antiochus III (209).

list.name: Mithridates I
list.note: Conquered Media and Mesopotamia; took Seleucia (141); captured Demetrius II.

list.name: Phraates II
list.note: Defeated and killed Antiochus VII (129); killed fighting Saka nomads and mutinous Greek captives.

list.name: Artabanus I
list.note: Killed fighting the Tocharians.

list.name: Mithridates II
list.note: Restored Parthian power; first contact with Rome at the Euphrates meeting with Sulla (96), whose seating humiliated the envoy Orobazus.

list.name: Phraates III
list.note: Dealt with Pompey; murdered by his sons.

list.name: Mithridates IV
list.note: Fled to Gabinius; executed by his brother Orodes.

list.name: Orodes II
list.note: Destroyed Crassus at Carrhae (53) through his general Surena; murdered by his son Phraates IV.

list.name: Pacorus I
list.note: Co-ruler; overran Syria with Labienus (40); killed by Ventidius at Gindarus.

list.name: Phraates IV
list.note: Defeated Antony (36); returned the standards of Carrhae (20); sent four sons to Rome as hostages; poisoned by his Italian wife Musa and son Phraataces.

list.name: Tiridates II
list.note: Pretender who fled to Augustus.

list.name: Phraates V (Phraataces)
list.note: Co-ruled with his mother Musa; agreed the Euphrates frontier with Gaius Caesar (AD 1).

list.name: Vonones I
list.note: Roman-educated hostage, rejected as too Roman.

list.name: Artabanus II
list.note: Expelled 35-36 by the Roman nominee Tiridates III.

list.name: Gotarzes II
list.note: Defeated the Roman-backed pretender Meherdates (49).

list.name: Vologases I
list.note: Installed Tiridates in Armenia; war with Corbulo; compromise of Rhandeia (63); founded Vologasias.

list.name: Artabanus III
list.note: Pretender who harboured a false Nero.

list.name: Osroes I
list.note: Lost Ctesiphon to Trajan (116), whose daughter he had held; Trajan crowned Parthamaspates.

list.name: Parthamaspates
list.note: Trajan's puppet; later king of Osrhoene.

list.name: Vologases IV
list.note: Invaded Armenia and Syria (161), provoking Lucius Verus' war; Ctesiphon and Seleucia sacked by Avidius Cassius (165).

list.name: Vologases V
list.note: Ctesiphon sacked by Septimius Severus (198).

list.name: Vologases VI
list.note: Rival of his brother Artabanus IV; last Arsacid coins c. 228.

list.name: Artabanus IV
list.note: Defeated Macrinus at Nisibis (217); killed by Ardashir at Hormozgan 28 Apr 224.

rulers.note: Numbering follows Encyclopaedia Iranica; dates before Mithridates I and in the 'Dark Age' (91-57 BC) are approximate.

rulers.title: Sasanian shahanshahs

list.name: Ardashir I
list.note: King of Persis from c. 208/211; victor at Hormozgan (224); crowned at Ctesiphon (226); attacked Roman Mesopotamia (230-232, 238-240).

list.name: Shapur I
list.note: Co-ruler from 240; defeated Gordian III (244), took Antioch (253 or 256) and captured Valerian (260); ŠKZ inscription; patron of Mani.

list.name: Bahram I
list.note: Had Mani executed (274 or 276) at Kartir's urging.

list.name: Bahram II
list.note: Lost Mesopotamia to Carus (283).

list.name: Bahram III
list.note: Overthrown by his great-uncle Narseh (Paikuli inscription).

list.name: Narseh
list.note: Defeated by Galerius (298); Peace of Nisibis ceded the five Transtigritane regions.

list.name: Hormizd II
list.note: Killed by Arabs while hunting, or in battle.

list.name: Adur Narseh
list.note: Killed by nobles after a few months.

list.name: Shapur II
list.note: 'Crowned in the womb'; 70-year reign; persecuted Christians from 340; besieged Amida (359); recovered Nisibis by Jovian's treaty (363).

list.name: Shapur III
list.note: Killed when nobles cut the ropes of his tent; partition of Armenia with Rome (c. 387).

list.name: Bahram IV
list.note: Killed by mutinous troops.

list.name: Yazdegerd I
list.note: Tolerant of Christians (synod of Seleucia-Ctesiphon 410); named guardian of Theodosius II by Arcadius (Procopius). Died in Hyrcania, by legend kicked by a magical horse; probably killed by nobles.

list.name: Shapur IV
list.note: Ex-king of Armenia; killed by nobles.

list.name: Bahram V Gur
list.note: Brief war with Rome (421-422); legendary hunter who disappeared into a swamp or quicksand while hunting.

list.name: Yazdegerd II
list.note: War with Rome (440); crushed the Armenian revolt at Avarayr (451).

list.name: Hormizd III
list.note: Killed by his brother Peroz.

list.name: Peroz I
list.note: Captured by the Hephthalites, ransomed; killed in a trench trap by them (484).

list.name: Balash
list.note: Blinded.

list.name: Kavad I
list.note: Deposed 496 (Mazdakite affair), escaped from the Fortress of Oblivion, restored 498/499 with Hephthalite help; wars with Rome 502-506 (took Amida) and 526-531.

list.name: Khosrow I Anushirvan
list.note: Fiscal and military reforms; Eternal Peace (532); sacked Antioch (540); Fifty Years' Peace (561/562); conquered Yemen (c. 570).

list.name: Hormizd IV
list.note: Deposed in a palace coup, blinded and killed.

list.name: Bahram VI Chobin
list.note: Mihranid general who took the throne; defeated by Khosrow II with Roman troops at the Blarathon (591).

list.name: Khosrow II Parviz
list.note: Restored by Maurice (591); used Maurice's murder as casus belli (603); conquered Syria, Jerusalem (614), Egypt (619); defeated by Heraclius (627). Deposed and executed 28 Feb 628.

list.name: Vistahm
list.note: Rebel king in the north-east (dates 591/595-596/600).

list.name: Kavad II (Sheroe)
list.note: Made peace with Heraclius; killed most of his brothers; died of plague.

list.name: Ardashir III
list.note: Child king killed by Shahrbaraz.

list.name: Shahrbaraz
list.note: General who had besieged Constantinople (626); usurped with Heraclius' backing; killed after 40 days.

list.name: Boran
list.note: Daughter of Khosrow II; first queen regnant; returned the True Cross. Second reign 631-632.

list.name: Azarmidokht
list.note: Sister of Boran.

list.name: Yazdegerd III
list.note: Lost al-Qadisiyya (636/637), Ctesiphon (637), Nahavand (642); killed by a miller near Merv (651).

rulers.note: Dates are standard (Iranica); the civil war of 628-632 saw some ten rulers.

list.name: Balamber
list.note: Named only by Jordanes; possibly legendary.

list.name: Uldin
list.note: Killed Gainas (400) and sent his head to Arcadius; ally of Stilicho against Radagaisus (406); defeated in Thrace 408.

list.name: Charaton
list.note: Visited by Olympiodorus.

list.name: Octar
list.note: Died of overeating on campaign against the Burgundians (Socrates).

list.name: Rua (Rugila)
list.note: Extracted 350 lb of gold a year from Constantinople; died, by Socrates' account, struck by lightning.

list.name: Bleda
list.note: Co-ruler with his brother; killed by Attila.

list.name: Attila
list.note: Treaty of Margus (435), Balkan campaigns (441-447, tribute raised to 2,100 lb a year), invasion of Gaul (Catalaunian Plains 451) and Italy (452). Died of a haemorrhage on his wedding night.

list.name: Ellac
list.note: Killed at the Nedao against the Gepids under Ardaric.

list.name: Dengizich
list.note: Killed by the Roman general Anagastes; his head was displayed in the Hippodrome in Constantinople.

list.name: Ernak
list.note: Settled in the Dobruja.

list.name: Athanaric
list.note: Iudex of the Thervingi; made peace with Valens on a boat in the Danube (369); persecuted Gothic Christians; died in Constantinople two weeks after being received by Theodosius.

list.name: Fritigern
list.note: Led the Goths across the Danube (376) and to victory at Adrianople (378); disappears from the sources c. 380.

list.name: Ermanaric
list.note: Ruled a large realm in the Pontic steppe; killed himself facing the Huns (Ammianus).

list.name: Vithimiris
list.note: Killed fighting the Huns and Alans.

list.name: Alatheus and Saphrax
list.note: Regents for Vithimiris' son Videric; their cavalry decided Adrianople.

rulers.title: Kings of the Visigoths before Toulouse

list.name: Alaric I
list.note: Sacked Rome 24-27 Aug 410; died at Consentia and was buried in the bed of the Busento.

list.name: Athaulf
list.note: Married Galla Placidia at Narbo (414); murdered in a stable at Barcino.

list.name: Sigeric
list.note: Reigned seven days.

list.name: Wallia
list.note: Returned Placidia for 600,000 measures of grain; fought the Vandals and Alans in Spain for Rome; settled in Aquitaine (418).

rulers.title: Kings of the Visigoths (Toulouse and Toledo)

list.name: Theodoric I
list.note: Killed at the Catalaunian Plains.

list.name: Thorismund
list.note: Killed by his brothers.

list.name: Theodoric II
list.note: Made Avitus emperor (455); described by Sidonius (Ep. 1.2); killed by his brother Euric.

list.name: Euric
list.note: Extended the kingdom to the Loire, Rhône and most of Spain; Code of Euric.

list.name: Alaric II
list.note: Breviary of Alaric (506); killed by Clovis at Vouillé.

list.name: Gesalec
list.note: Driven out by Ostrogothic forces.

list.name: Amalaric
list.note: Under Theodoric the Great's tutelage until 526; killed at Barcino after defeat by Childebert I.

list.name: Theudis
list.note: Ostrogothic general; failed attack on Septem (Ceuta).

list.name: Theudigisel
list.note: Killed at a banquet in Seville.

list.name: Agila I
list.note: Killed by his own men after Athanagild's revolt brought in Byzantine troops (Spania).

list.name: Athanagild
list.note: Moved the capital to Toledo; father of Brunhild and Galswintha.

list.name: Liuvigild
list.note: Reunified Spain, annexed the Suebic kingdom (585), executed his Catholic son Hermenegild (585).

list.name: Reccared I
list.note: Converted to Catholicism (587; Third Council of Toledo 589).

list.name: Liuva II
list.note: Hand cut off and killed by Witteric.

list.name: Witteric
list.note: Killed at a banquet.

list.name: Sisebut
list.note: Scholar-king, correspondent of Isidore; forced conversion of Jews; took most of Byzantine Spania. Death by illness or poison.

list.name: Suintila
list.note: Expelled the last Byzantine garrisons (c. 625).

list.name: Sisenand
list.note: Fourth Council of Toledo (633).

list.name: Tulga
list.note: Tonsured and sent to a monastery by Chindasuinth.

rulers.title: Amal kings of the Ostrogoths before Italy

list.name: Valamir
list.note: Fought for Attila at the Catalaunian Plains; settled in Pannonia after Nedao; killed fighting the Sciri.

list.name: Theodemir
list.note: Father of Theodoric; moved the Goths into the Balkans (473).

list.name: Theodoric the Great (before Italy)
list.note: Hostage in Constantinople (461-471); consul 484; sent by Zeno against Odoacer (488).

list.name: Theodoric the Great
list.note: Killed Odoacer with his own hands (15 Mar 493); ruled Italy as king with a Roman administration (Cassiodorus, Boethius, executed 524). Mausoleum at Ravenna.

list.name: Athalaric
list.note: Grandson of Theodoric, under his mother's regency; died of drink aged 18.

list.name: Amalasuntha
list.note: Regent 526-534, queen 534; negotiated secretly with Justinian; strangled in her bath on Lake Bolsena, giving Justinian his casus belli.

list.name: Theodahad
list.note: Killed after failing to stop Belisarius taking Naples.

list.name: Witiges
list.note: Besieged Rome (537-538); surrendered at Ravenna (540).
list.death: natural, at Constantinople as a patrician

list.name: Ildibad
list.note: Killed by a Gepid bodyguard.

list.name: Eraric
list.note: Rugian king killed after five months.

list.name: Totila (Baduila)
list.note: Retook almost all Italy, took Rome twice (546, 550); mortally wounded at Busta Gallorum/Taginae against Narses.

list.name: Teia
list.note: Killed at Mons Lactarius near Vesuvius.

list.name: Odoacer
list.note: Scirian officer who deposed Romulus Augustulus and sent the regalia to Zeno; rex in Italy; killed by Theodoric at a banquet in Ravenna.

list.name: Godigisel
list.note: Killed by Franks before the Rhine crossing.

list.name: Gunderic
list.note: Led the Vandals across the Rhine (31 Dec 406) and into Spain (409); took Hispalis.

list.name: Gaiseric
list.note: Crossed to Africa (429) with c. 80,000 people; took Carthage 19 Oct 439; sacked Rome (455); destroyed Leo I's armada (468); treaty of 474 with Zeno.

list.name: Huneric
list.note: Married Eudocia, daughter of Valentinian III; persecuted Catholics.

list.name: Thrasamund
list.note: Married Theodoric's sister Amalafrida.

list.name: Hilderic
list.note: Pro-Roman, pro-Catholic grandson of Valentinian III.
list.death: executed by Gelimer when Belisarius landed

list.name: Gelimer
list.note: Defeated at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum (533); surrendered on Mount Papua (534); walked in Belisarius' triumph and retired to estates in Galatia.

list.name: Chlodio
list.note: Took Cambrai and the land to the Somme; defeated by Aetius at Vicus Helena.

list.name: Merovech
list.note: Eponym of the Merovingians; perhaps legendary.

list.name: Childeric I
list.note: Federate king at Tournai, fought alongside Aegidius and Count Paul; his grave (found 1653) held a signet ring and a crossbow brooch of a Roman official.

rulers.title: Merovingian kings of the Franks

list.name: Clovis I
list.note: Defeated Syagrius at Soissons (486), the Alamanni (Tolbiac, c. 496/506), the Visigoths at Vouillé (507); Catholic baptism at Reims (496 or 508); honorary consul from Anastasius (508); Lex Salica.

list.name: Theuderic I
list.note: Reims/Metz.

list.name: Chlodomer
list.note: Orléans; killed at Vézeronce against the Burgundians.

list.name: Childebert I
list.note: Paris.

list.name: Chlothar I
list.note: Soissons; sole king 558-561.

list.name: Theudebert I
list.note: Invaded Italy (539); struck gold coins in his own name, outraging Procopius.

list.name: Charibert I
list.note: Paris.

list.name: Guntram
list.note: Burgundy; later venerated as a saint.

list.name: Sigebert I
list.note: Austrasia; husband of Brunhild; killed by assassins of Fredegund.

list.name: Chilperic I
list.note: Neustria; husband of Fredegund; stabbed returning from a hunt.

list.name: Chlothar II
list.note: Sole king 613 after executing Brunhild; Edict of Paris (614).

list.name: Theudebert II
list.note: Killed after defeat by his brother.

list.name: Theuderic II
list.note: Died of dysentery at Metz.

list.name: Sigebert II
list.note: Child king killed by Chlothar II.

list.name: Dagobert I
list.note: Austrasia 623, sole king 629-634; founded Saint-Denis; the last strong Merovingian.

list.name: Charibert II
list.note: Aquitaine; possibly murdered.

list.name: Sigebert III
list.note: Austrasia.

list.name: Clovis II
list.note: Neustria and Burgundy.

rulers.note: Divided kingdoms: Reims/Austrasia, Orléans/Burgundy, Paris, Soissons/Neustria.

list.name: Wacho
list.note: Lething dynasty; marriage alliances with Thuringians, Gepids and Franks.

list.name: Audoin
list.note: Settled in Pannonia as Byzantine allies; sent 5,500 men to Narses (552).

list.name: Alboin
list.note: Destroyed the Gepids with the Avars (567), killing Cunimund and making a drinking cup of his skull; invaded Italy (568); killed at Verona at the instigation of his wife Rosamund, Cunimund's daughter.

list.name: Cleph
list.note: Killed by a slave; ten years of rule by the dukes followed (574-584).

list.name: Authari
list.note: Restored the monarchy; married Theodelinda. Possibly poisoned.

list.name: Agilulf
list.note: Catholic sympathies via Theodelinda; peace with the exarchate.

list.name: Arioald
list.note: Arian.

list.name: Rothari
list.note: Took Liguria and Opitergium from the exarchate; Edictum Rothari (643).

list.name: Gundahar
list.note: Settled on the Rhine (Worms) as foederati; with Goar backed Jovinus; destroyed by Aetius' Hunnic auxiliaries (436/437), the kernel of the Nibelungenlied.

list.name: Gundioc
list.note: Kingdom resettled in Sapaudia (443); magister militum.

list.name: Chilperic I (Burgundian)
list.note: Brother of Gundioc.

list.name: Gundobad
list.note: Killed Anthemius for Ricimer (472); briefly magister militum and kingmaker in Italy (Glycerius); Lex Burgundionum (Liber Constitutionum).

list.name: Godegisel
list.note: Killed at Vienne by Gundobad.

list.name: Sigismund
list.note: Converted to Catholicism; founded Saint-Maurice d'Agaune; captured and thrown down a well by Chlodomer.

list.name: Godomar
list.note: Defeated Chlodomer at Vézeronce (524); kingdom conquered by the Franks (534).

rulers.title: Kings of the Sueves in Gallaecia

list.name: Hermeric
list.note: Led the Sueves into Gallaecia; abdicated in illness (438).

list.name: Rechila
list.note: Took Emerita (439) and Hispalis (441).

list.name: Rechiar
list.note: First Catholic Germanic king; defeated by Theodoric II at the Urbicus and executed.

list.name: Remismund
list.note: Turned Arian; the sources then fall silent until c. 550.

list.name: Theodemar
list.note: Catholic again (Martin of Braga); Councils of Braga (561, 572).

list.name: Andeca
list.note: Liuvigild annexed the kingdom (585).

list.name: Ardaric
list.note: Attila's favourite; led the revolt that destroyed the Huns at the Nedao (454).

list.name: Thurisind
list.note: Wars with the Lombards over Sirmium.

list.name: Cunimund
list.note: Killed by Alboin; the Gepid kingdom destroyed by Lombards and Avars.

rulers.title: Khagans of the Avars

list.name: Bayan I
list.note: Led the Avars into the Carpathian basin (568); took Sirmium (582); exacted rising tribute from Constantinople (80,000 to 120,000 solidi a year).

list.name: Son of Bayan (unnamed)
list.note: Ambush of Heraclius near Heraclea (617).

list.name: Khagan of the siege of 626 (unnamed)
list.note: Besieged Constantinople with Slavs and Persians (Jul-Aug 626); after the failure Avar hegemony over the Slavs and Bulgars collapsed (Samo, Kubrat).

rulers.note: Avar khagans are often unnamed in the sources; the names of Bayan's successors are unknown.

list.name: Agron
list.note: Built the Illyrian navy; died celebrating a victory over the Aetolians.

list.name: Teuta
list.note: Regent for Pinnes; her piracy and the murder of a Roman envoy provoked the First Illyrian War (229); peace of 228.

list.name: Pleuratus
list.note: Roman ally.

list.name: Genthius
list.note: Sided with Perseus; captured by Anicius in 30 days (168); led in triumph.

list.name: Burebista
list.note: United Getae and Dacians; ally of Pompey; murdered c. 44, the same year as Caesar who planned to attack him.

list.name: Duras
list.note: Ceded power to Decebalus.

list.name: Decebalus
list.note: Defeated Cornelius Fuscus (86/87); fought Domitian and Trajan; cut his throat to avoid capture (106), scene shown on Trajan's Column; his head was brought to Rome by Tiberius Claudius Maximus (Philippi tombstone).

list.name: Odaenathus
list.note: Exarch of Palmyra; routed Shapur's army returning from Edessa (260), crushed Quietus, invaded Persia (262-263, 266); styled King of Kings and corrector totius Orientis; murdered at Emesa with his son Herodian.

list.name: Zenobia
list.note: Regent for Vaballathus; took Egypt (270) and Asia Minor; Augusta 272; defeated at Immae and Emesa; captured fleeing to the Euphrates.
list.death: lived at Tibur according to the HA; or died on the way to Rome (Zosimus)

list.name: Abu Bakr
list.note: Ridda wars; first raids on Roman Palestine (battle of Ajnadayn, Jul 634).

list.name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
list.note: Conquest of Syria (Damascus 635, Yarmuk Aug 636), Jerusalem (637/638), Iraq, Egypt (from 639); stabbed by the Persian slave Abu Lu'lu'a.

list.name: Uthman ibn Affan
list.note: Standardized the Quran; killed by rebels in Medina.

list.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
list.note: Killed at Kufa by a Kharijite.
